messages:
maria: quick heads-up — we need to lock down the quant-profile packaging & naming before we push the Optimize UI change. Current experiments are all over the place.

sam: +1. can you sketch a minimal manifest and a recommended filename pattern? i want the rollout script to validate it.

maria: high-level goals: 1) make optimizer suggestions ID-stable (so Optimize can point to a profile), 2) make it easy to tell backend/bitwidth at a glance, 3) include eval deltas and deploy tags for routing.

jonah: agree. i've been surfacing experiments with AWQ and GPTQ for the same model and it's messy to compare. would help if the profile records the quant pipeline (e.g., per-layer heuristics).

maria: exactly — propose a filename pattern: `<model>-<backend>-<bits>-<calib>-v<semver>.qpkg`  e.g. `mistral-7b-awq-4x8-calibA-v0.2.qpkg`

lisa: can we avoid embedding long calib names? maybe short codes for calibs and a manifesto file inside the package with full meta.

maria: yep. package layout idea: \n```\n/manifest.json  # flat metadata (fields below)\n/quant.bin      # binary payload (gptq/awq artifacts)\n/evals/         # per-prompt eval results (csv/json)\n/docs/          # notes from measurement runs\n```\n
maria: manifest fields (minimal): `model`, `backend`, `bitwidth`, `quant_pipeline`, `calib_code`, `semver`, `accuracy_delta`, `latency_p50_ms`, `cost_est_tokens`, `stability_score`, `deploy_tags`

devon: what's `stability_score`?

maria: heuristic between 0-1 combining variance across eval sets, flaky logits, and failure modes (divergence on long context). used by Optimize to warn on risky profiles.

sam: how do we represent accuracy deltas? per-eval-suite or aggregated?

jonah: both. in manifest: `accuracy_delta` (aggregated like `-0.5%` relative to base), and `eval_breakdown` linking to files in `/evals/` with per-suite delta and sample counts.

lisa: will Optimize recommend auto-fallbacks? e.g., if latency or delta exceed thresholds, route to compatible profile or FP16.

maria: plan: Optimize will surface 3 ranked profiles per workload — "recommended", "fallback-low-cost", "fallback-high-accuracy" — plus a compatibility list of model variants. the profiles returned will reference package IDs that match our filename + semver.

opt-bot: automation note: when new qpkg lands in the storage bucket, opt-bot will validate manifest schema and post a summary to #eng-ml with a quick badge (pass/warn/fail).

sam: schema validation specs? we should include a JSON Schema and a small CLI `qpkg-validate` that CI can run.

maria: will draft schema. minimal required keys: `model`, `backend`, `bitwidth`, `semver`, `accuracy_delta`, `latency_p50_ms`, `deploy_tags`. optional: `eval_breakdown`, `quant_pipeline`, `stability_score`, `notes_url`.

devon: naming collisions concern: semver handles updates, but what if two teams create profiles for same `model-backend-bits` with different calibs? filename includes calib_code so unique. Also we should enforce an owner field in manifest.

maria: good call — add `owner` and `approved_by` fields for Dedicated/Private rollouts.

jonah: rollout flow idea: \n1) author uploads qpkg to staging bucket with `draft` semver (e.g., v0.0)\n2) opt-bot validates and posts results\n3) ML lead approves -> bump to `v0.1` and promote to shared bucket\n4) Optimize periodic job indexes new packages and runs quick smoke evals to double-check accuracy_delta\n5) if smoke passes, label `recommended` for cost/latency window

lisa: can we embed `deploy_profiles` array in manifest to indicate intended targets, e.g. `["hosted:low-latency","dedicated:throughput"]`? Optimize will use that to filter suggestions.

maria: yes — `deploy_tags` will be freeform but we should maintain a canonical list in repo so Optimize can map tag -> routing policy.

sam: action items: maria to write schema + sample qpkg; sam to add `qpkg-validate` to infra repo; opt-bot owner to wire storage hook. timeline: aim for draft by EOD Thursday.

maria: sounds good. i'll post the sample manifest in this thread when ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
